falsifier: Any MWCC-1.2.5 function in which (a) reordering a byte-typed local past a word-sized local within one declaration list CHANGES the callee-saved numbering - which would show the classes are not disjoint and that width is a tiebreak rather than a partition; or (b) retyping a byte local to int with an explicit (u8) truncating cast changes the instruction count or the opcode multiset - which would make the lever non-free and cost-bearing rather than a pure recolor; or (c) a function whose narrow locals are numbered BELOW its word-sized locals, which would refute the class ORDER while leaving the partition standing. Evidence lives in the aligned view: python tools/gdl/fnasm.py <unit> <fn> --diff plus python tools/gdl/composed_census/wf_word_diff.py <unit> <fn> before and after the reorder or retype. Re-running the three probes behind this law on game/movie/movieplayer.cpp::fn_800D8BCC at commits 707b4feb1 and 056c19f25 reproduces it.
subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
SCOPE AND STANDING. This EXTENDS claim.law.SP_initializer-presence-outranks-declaration-position-in-callee-saved-numbering.20260901.v1 with a second, orthogonal grouping key. That law found MWCC hands out callee-saved GPRs downward from r31 in two passes decided ahead of the declaration sequence - initialised-at-declaration locals first, then uninitialised ones, each in declaration order. It could not see the key recorded here because its measurement function (show_piles) has no narrow-typed locals at all.

THE RULE. NARROW (BYTE-TYPED) LOCALS ARE NUMBERED AS THEIR OWN CLASS, AHEAD OF EVERY WORD-SIZED LOCAL, REGARDLESS OF DECLARATION POSITION. Declaration order orders locals only WITHIN a width class. Measured on game/movie/movieplayer.cpp::fn_800D8BCC at commit 707b4feb1, a count-symmetric 215/215 function in which NOT ONE of the ten locals carries a declaration initializer - so all ten sit in SP's second group and SP's own split cannot explain the layout. With the declaration list `u8 sh1; u8 sh0; u8 sh2; u8* p; int n; int i; int off; u8* pal; u8* ip; int count;` the assignment was sh1=r31, sh0=r30, sh2=r29, p=r28, n=r27, i=r26, pal=r25, ip=r24, count=r23 - strictly monotone descending with declaration position, but only after the three u8s had taken the top three whatever their position.

THE CROSS-CLASS REORDER IS A CATEGORICAL NULL. Moving `u8* p; int n; int i;` ABOVE the three u8 shifts in the same declaration list produced a BYTE-IDENTICAL object - not a shifted register, not a reordered instruction. This is the same signature SP records for a cross-group reorder and it is the diagnostic that tells you a width boundary, not a position, is holding the layout: if reordering two locals past each other changes NOTHING in the object, they are in different classes and no further reordering will ever move them past each other.

THE ONLY LEVER ACROSS THE BOUNDARY IS THE DECLARED TYPE, AND IT IS FREE. Retyping `u8 sh0/sh1/sh2` to `int` while respelling the assignments with an explicit truncating cast - `sh1 = (u8)(8 - state->greenBits);` - moved all three from r31/r30/r29 down to r28/r27/r26 and lifted p/n/i to r31/r30/r29, reproducing the target's numbering exactly. THE INSTRUCTION STREAM IS UNCHANGED BY THE RETYPE: MWCC emits the same `clrlwi rD,rS,24` for an explicit (u8) cast into an int as it does for the implicit truncation on assignment into a u8, so the instruction count, the opcode multiset and every mnemonic hold while only the numbering moves. Measured payoff on fn_800D8BCC: differing words 105 -> 95, real 208 -> 184, fresh per-function objdiff fuzzy 94.9070 -> 95.1628, count held 215/215 and multiset held at 4 tokens, i.e. the retype is a pure recolor. Commit 056c19f25.

SCOPE BOUNDARY WORTH THE RECORD, because it contradicts a natural reading of a neighbouring law. claim.law.block-allocation-order-is-textual-not-nesting-depth.20260831.v1 establishes that for STACK SLOTS the one available scope lever is function scope versus inner scope, and that moving a declaration across that boundary relocates it. THAT DOES NOT TRANSFER TO CALLEE-SAVED REGISTER NUMBERING. Hoisting seven inner-block locals from a `case 2: { ... }` compound statement to function scope, preserving their relative order, produced a BYTE-IDENTICAL object here. For locals that already hold callee-saved registers, the scope boundary carries no weight in the numbering; width and declaration position carry all of it. Do not spend a probe on a scope hoist to renumber a register.

THE SCREEN, before spending a build. Derive the FULL target-to-ours callee-saved correspondence first and write both sequences out descending from r31 - a rotation or a block swap between the two lists is the tell for this law, and it is invisible in an --ops multiset, which reported this whole 24-word layout defect as zero tokens. Then: if the two lists hold the same locals in the same relative order within each width class and differ only by which class sits on top, the cure is a RETYPE, not a reorder. If they differ within a class, reorder inside that class and expect roughly one register per position, per SP. If reordering two locals is byte-identical, stop reordering them: they are in different classes.

MEASUREMENT NOTE. All probes behind this law held 215/215 with an unchanged 4-token multiset, so `real` and the raw differing-WORD count from tools/gdl/composed_census/wf_word_diff.py were the only moving instruments and no obligation-size differencing was involved. The word count is the honest instrument for this class: an --ops multiset is blind to pure register-field words by construction, and on this function it read an identical 4 tokens across a 119 -> 95 word improvement.
